_about: Embraer 195, from APM 1997 Rev 11 (Oct 09/15; the figure Oct 07/08) Figure 2.1 General Aircraft Dimensions (page index 33): side, plan and front views on one sheet, black vector lines. Unlike the E190's figure, drawn to one scale both ways (its printed 38.67 m length, 28.72 m span and 10.57 m height agree within 0.3%), so no --xscale. Scaled by the printed 38.67 m overall length, nose to tail cone. The E190's (e190/) points moved by the two fuselage plugs (plug.py: 0.81 m ahead of the wing, from the printed nose-to-main-gear 14.64 m against 13.83 m; 1.62 m behind it, from the aft door's move), then snapped to this sheet. Pixels of layers.py rasters at scale 16, line centres. Windows joined to other lines (the overwing exit's own; one crossed by the winglet's lines) and one hidden behind the winglet (placed midway between its neighbours) are listed in windowsAlso.

sources.title: Embraer, Embraer 195 Airport Planning Manual (APM 1997 Rev 11, Oct 09/15), Section 2, Figure 2.1 General Aircraft Dimensions; 2.5 cabin cross-section
sources.note: Read from the Internet Archive's copy of 2024-10-08 (web.archive.org/web/20241008225517/...): Embraer's link now goes nowhere. Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views (tools/trace/e195/); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing.
